issues.t: CVT failure, jerking or slipping
issues.sym: Jerking, shuddering, the engine revving high without the car speeding up, a whining noise, or the car going into a low-power limp mode.
issues.why: Most Jukes use a continuously variable transmission (CVT). Transmission failure is one of the most-reported Juke problems, often around 60,000 to 80,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the CVT fluid checked and changed on schedule. If it slips or goes into limp mode, get a diagnosis right away and ask Nissan about any goodwill or extended coverage.

issues.t: Turbocharger fails
issues.sym: Loss of power, blue-gray smoke, burning oil, a whistle or grinding from the engine, and boost codes such as P0299.
issues.why: The small turbocharger spins very fast and relies on clean oil. Worn bearings, often from late oil changes or oil feed problems, make it fail; debris can then hurt the engine.
issues.next: Stop hard driving and have it checked quickly. A failing turbo can send metal into the engine. Change oil often with the correct synthetic oil.

issues.t: Engine failure needing replacement
issues.sym: Knocking, heavy oil use, loss of power or the engine seizing, followed by a dealer recommending a new engine.
issues.why: Owners report full engine failures, often linked to oil starvation, turbo debris or timing chain damage on this small turbo engine.
issues.next: Keep oil changes short and check the oil level between changes. If the engine starts knocking, stop driving it to limit damage.

issues.t: Won't start from a drained battery
issues.sym: The car will not crank or start, especially after sitting a day or two; the battery keeps going dead.
issues.why: No-start is the most-reported problem for the 2012 Juke. A common cause is a parasitic electrical draw, often traced to the key switch circuit or a water-damaged power distribution module.
issues.next: Have the battery tested, then have a shop measure the draw with the car off to find which circuit is staying awake.

issues.t: A/C blows warm when stopped
issues.sym: The air conditioning cools while driving but blows warm when idling or in traffic. The engine may run hot.
issues.why: RepairPal lists this as the most common Juke problem, usually from a failed cooling fan and sometimes a damaged coolant hose.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge. Have the cooling fan and hoses checked soon, since the same fan keeps the engine cool.

issues.t: Airbag light flashes
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) warning light flashes or stays on.
issues.why: RepairPal lists a constantly flashing airbag light as a common Juke problem. Common causes are seat or under-seat wiring connectors and sensors.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. The airbags may not work properly while the light is on.

issues.t: Stalls or loses power while driving
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses acceleration or shuts off in traffic or on the highway.
issues.why: Owners report misfires, a failed airflow sensor or traction control faults as causes.
issues.next: Have codes read right away and pull over safely if power drops.

issues.t: Sunroof glass shatters
issues.sym: The sunroof glass breaks suddenly with no obvious impact, sometimes while driving.
issues.why: Owners have reported sunroof glass shattering on its own.
issues.next: Close the sunshade, pull over and cover the opening. Report it to Nissan and NHTSA.

issues.t: Fuel pressure sensor can leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell around the engine, or a small fuel leak.
issues.why: The fuel pressure sensor may not have been tightened enough and can loosen from heat and vibration, leaking fuel near hot parts. Recalls 12V069, 14V683 and 18V156 (to redo some earlier repairs).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you smell fuel, do not drive it and have it towed.

issues.t: Start button can stick and shut off engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, often after the push-button start sticks in hot weather.
issues.why: The engine start/stop button can stick in its housing, and road bumps can then switch the engine off. Recall 15V418.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and get the free repair.

issues.t: Rear seatback latch weld may break (recall)
issues.sym: No obvious symptom in normal use.
issues.why: An incomplete weld may let the rear seatback striker separate in a crash, so the seatback may not stay latched. Recall 12V328.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the free repair.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can leak into booster (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels soft and the car takes longer to stop.
issues.why: A master cylinder problem can leak brake fluid into the brake booster, reducing braking. Recall 18V086 covers NISMO RS models.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN. If the pedal feels soft, do not drive until it is inspected.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch, rattle and check engine light
issues.sym: A rattle or unusual engine noise, the check engine light coming on, rough running or stalling. If the chain breaks, the engine stops and may be badly damaged.
issues.why: On 2011-2013 Jukes the timing chain can wear and stretch over time. Nissan ran a service campaign (P4213, bulletin NTB14-030) to replace the chain, guides and crank sprocket, but that campaign has ended and owners still report failures, sometimes after the campaign repair.
issues.next: If you hear a new rattle or the check engine light comes on, have the codes read and the timing chain checked soon. Fixing a stretched chain early can prevent engine damage. Ask Nissan whether the campaign was done on your car.

issues.t: Fuel pump or fuel level sender fails
issues.sym: Hard starting or no start, stalling or loss of power, a check engine light, or a fuel gauge that reads wrong.
issues.why: Owners report failed high- and low-pressure fuel pumps, a failed fuel pump relay, and a failed fuel tank sending unit (the part that reports the fuel level).
issues.next: Have a shop test fuel pressure and read the codes before replacing parts, since a faulty relay can cause the same no-start. Do not rely on the gauge if it reads wrong; refuel early.

issues.t: Check engine light for evaporative (EVAP) leak
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with codes such as P0456, P0455 or P0442. The car usually drives normally.
issues.why: The fuel vapor system has a small leak. Nissan bulletins point to a loose or worn gas cap and a leaking O-ring at the EVAP vent control valve.
issues.next: First make sure the gas cap clicks tight. If the light returns, have the EVAP system smoke-tested and ask about bulletin NTB17-082.

issues.t: Clicking from axles when pulling away
issues.sym: A clicking or ticking noise from the front or rear wheels when you accelerate from a stop.
issues.why: Nissan bulletin NTB12-055 covers clicking from the axle shafts on take-off. The usual fix is cleaning and adding special grease where the axle meets the wheel hub; a worn CV joint needs a new axle.
issues.next: Have a shop check whether the noise comes from the axle-to-hub joint or a worn CV joint. A torn CV boot or clicking while turning means the axle should be replaced soon.

issues.t: Clunk from top of front strut when steering
issues.sym: A clunk, pop or bump from the front corners when turning the steering wheel, especially at low speed.
issues.why: Nissan bulletin NTB14088B covers this noise from the top of the front strut, where the strut mount and bearing sit.
issues.next: Have the front strut mounts and suspension checked. It is usually not urgent, but a loose suspension part should be ruled out.

issues.t: Door won't lock or unlock from outside handle button
issues.sym: Pressing the lock/unlock button on the outside door handle does nothing, or the front door latch freezes in cold weather.
issues.why: Nissan bulletins cover an unresponsive request button on the outside handle (NTB-13-038) and front door latches that can freeze, which were greased and sealed under campaign P1264 (now ended).
issues.next: Use the key fob buttons in the meantime. Ask a dealer whether the bulletins apply; the button or handle may need to be replaced.

issues.t: Worn tie rod ends cause clunk or loose steering
issues.sym: A clunk over bumps, loose or wandering steering, or uneven tire wear on the front tires.
issues.why: Tie rod ends are one of the most-reported Juke repairs in TrueDelta's owner survey. They are the joints that connect the steering rack to the wheels.
issues.next: Have the steering checked soon, since a badly worn tie rod can affect control. Tie rods are sold separately; you rarely need a whole new steering system. Get an alignment after the repair.

issues.t: Turbo air inlet tube can separate and stall engine (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, the check engine light on, and the engine possibly stalling at idle.
issues.why: On some early 2011 Jukes the turbocharger air inlet tube and boost sensor can come apart, putting the engine in a low-power fail-safe mode. Recall 11V583.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls. If power drops suddenly, pull over safely and have it inspected.
